newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Q1 oil deficit grows 53.1 percent on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Q1 oil deficit grows 53.1 percent on 1996.

text.p: Peru posted an oil and derivatives trade deficit of $100 million in the first quarter 1997, up 53.1 percent from $65 million in the same 1996 period, the Central Bank said Tuesday.
The bank's weekly report also showed a $29 million deficit in March, compared with a $18 million deficit in the same month last year.
Peru imported oil and derivatives worth $189 million in the January-March period, a rise of 13.6 percent against $166 million in the same period last year.
Exports fell 11.9 percent in the first quarter to $89 million from $101 million in the same 1996 period.
Peru reported an oil deficit of $347 million last year, up 11 percent on the previous year.
